subject: MSA/order form: clarifying output attribution, training & telemetry gating
messages:
From: Priya Shah <priya.shah@altumtech.com>
To: sean_gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
Cc: Darin Cole <darin@altumtech.com>, procurement@altumtech.com
Date: Sat, 29 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: MSA / Order Form questions — output attribution & telemetry gating

Hi Sean,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. Procurement is starting the MSA + order form review and we have a few specific concerns from Legal/ML Ops about the IP & training language before we can move to signatures:

- Output attribution: we need clarity whether Altum will have exclusive rights to model outputs that are "productized" (i.e., included in our product) and whether Redwood will make any downstream claims.
- Training / data use: the draft states Redwood may "use feedback and telemetry to improve services" — can you confirm whether that includes training or fine-tuning models on Altum-provided prompts, logs, or outputs?
- Feedback license: procurement wants a narrow license that allows Redwood to operate and improve service reliability but not to include customer content in model training without explicit opt-in.

Could you share Redwood's proposed compromise language or a redline? Our procurement cycle is tight (we're aiming to finish legal review by 2026-09-03). If easier, can we set up a 20-min call early next week?

Thanks,
Priya Shah
Head of Product Ops | Altum Tech
priya.shah@altumtech.com

Attachment: altum_procurement_checklist.pdf (1 page)
From: sean_gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Priya Shah <priya.shah@altumtech.com>
Cc: Darin Cole <darin@altumtech.com>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, priyom_das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 29 Aug 2026 11:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MSA / Order Form questions — output attribution & telemetry gating

Hi Priya — appreciate the clear list. High level position from Redwood: we do not claim ownership of customer content or customer outputs. Practically that means:

- Output rights: Altum retains rights to outputs you receive from the service and can productize those outputs. Redwood won't assert title to your outputs.
- Training: Redwood's default stance is to use aggregated telemetry (metrics, anonymized usage patterns) to improve platform reliability and safety. We do not train customer-facing models on identifiable customer content without an explicit opt-in.
- Feedback license: we can propose a narrow operational feedback license limited to (a) service improvements, safety/abuse detection, and (b) aggregated telemetry for product analytics. Training/fine-tuning on raw customer content would require an explicit opt-in checkbox and SOW.

Suggested compromise (we'll send a redline for the MSA/order form): include a short clause that says "Redwood will not use Customer Content to train or improve Redwood models that are redistributed to other customers except with Customer's explicit opt-in. Redwood may retain aggregated, non-identifying telemetry for service reliability and safety."

I'll loop in Laura with a proposed redline and ask Product/Platform (Priyom) to confirm the telemetry gating mechanics (e.g., a customer-facing no-train flag for Dedicated/Private). Attaching an initial redline: altum_redlines_v1.docx.

If that sounds reasonable, let's do a 20 min call Mon/Tue to close.

Best,
Sean Gallagher
Senior Account Exec | Redwood Inference
sean_gallagher@redwood.com

Attachment: altum_redlines_v1.docx (MSA + order form markups)
From: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Priya Shah <priya.shah@altumtech.com>, sean_gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, priyom_das <priyom_das@redwood.com>, Darin Cole <darin@altumtech.com>
Date: Sat, 29 Aug 2026 13:28:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MSA / Order Form questions — output attribution & telemetry gating

Thanks Priya / Sean — looping in legal. Quick notes on the redline approach and risks: 

1) Output attribution: we can add explicit language that Customer retains all rights in Customer Content and in Outputs produced from Customer Content; Redwood will not assert ownership. That will satisfy productization asks.

2) Training carveout: propose two options in the contract: (A) default: Redwood may use aggregated, de-identified telemetry for product improvements; (B) opt-out: Customer may elect a "no-train" carveout in the order form that prohibits use of Customer Content for model training or fine-tuning. Option B should be priced (we'll include implications for model quality improvements and cost).

3) Feedback license: to satisfy procurement, narrow the license to the minimal words required for operation & safety. Example language: "Customer grants Redwood a non-exclusive, worldwide, royalty-free license to use Feedback solely to maintain and operate the Service and to improve performance, provided such use will not include training of models on identifiable Customer Content without Customer's express written consent."

4) Auditability / evidence: procurement may request evidence (audit logs, retention policy) that training exclusions are enforced. We should commit to producing audit logs for Dedicated/Private; for Hosted we can provide an attestation and operational controls. We should surface this to Security/Compliance if they need to prepare a short attestation pack.

I'll prepare a tracked redline with the two carveout options. Priyom / Product — please confirm feasibility for a configurable "no-train" flag and what we can ship quickly for Hosted vs Dedicated.

Laura Bennett
Head of Legal | Redwood Inference
laura_bennett@redwood.com

Attachment: altum_msa_redline_v2.docx (tracked changes, includes audit/logging commitments)
From: Darin Cole <darin@altumtech.com>
To: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, sean_gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Shah <priya.shah@altumtech.com>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, priyom_das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 30 Aug 2026 16:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MSA / Order Form questions — output attribution & telemetry gating

Laura / Sean — thanks for the quick turnaround and the two-option approach. Procurement and ML Ops reviewed and our asks are fairly narrow:

- We are willing to accept aggregated telemetry for reliability (logs/metrics) but we need a firm contractual prohibition on using Customer Content, Outputs, or prompts for training or re-distribution without explicit consent.
- The "no-train" carveout is acceptable as a priced option. For Hosted production, we need a short attestation and an operational playbook describing how Redwood enforces the no-train setting.

I attached our procurement checklist for context. If you can send a final redline with the two options and a short summary of enforcement (audit logs / attestation timelines), we can move this to final review — target internal sign-off by 2026-09-03.

Also proposed: 20-minute sync Mon 2026-08-31 10:00 AM PT to align legal / ML Ops (Priyom on product feasibility). Can you confirm?

Thanks,
Darin Cole
VP, Platform Engineering | Altum Tech
